theory.intro: Many functions need more than one rule at once. Identify the outermost structure, a product, a quotient or a power, and apply that rule first. Any inner derivative that is itself composite is then found with the chain rule.
facts: Identify the outermost structure first, product, quotient or composite power, because that sets the main rule.
With the product rule $y' = u'v + uv'$, differentiate any composite factor using the chain rule.
With the quotient rule $y' = \dfrac{u'v - uv'}{v^{2}}$, use the chain rule whenever $u$ or $v$ is composite.
For $y = \left(\dfrac{u}{v}\right)^{n}$, the chain rule gives $y' = n\left(\dfrac{u}{v}\right)^{n-1} \times \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{u}{v}\right)$, whose inner derivative needs the quotient rule.
Finally, factorise the result by taking out the highest common factor of any shared binomial bases.
steps: Identify the primary (outermost) operation: product, quotient, or outer power.
Apply the primary rule formula, setting aside sub-derivatives to compute.
Use the chain, product, or quotient rule to compute each required sub-derivative.
Substitute the sub-derivatives into the main formula.
Factorise common terms and simplify algebraic expressions to lowest terms.

workedExamples.question_text: Differentiate $y=3x^{2}(2x+1)^{4}$ using the product and chain rules. Factorise your answer completely.
Differentiate $y=4x\sqrt{3x+2}$ using the product and chain rules. Write your answer over a single denominator.
Differentiate $y=\dfrac{(2x+1)^{3}}{(x-1)^{2}}$ using the quotient and chain rules. Factorise your answer completely.
Differentiate $y=\dfrac{x+2}{\sqrt{2x+3}}$ using the quotient and chain rules.
Differentiate (a) $y=\left(\dfrac{2x+1}{x+3}\right)^{3}$ and (b) $y=\sqrt{\dfrac{2x+1}{x+3}}$ for $x>0$, using the chain and quotient rules.
workedExamples.solution_text:
For both parts, let $u=\dfrac{2x+1}{x+3}$.
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{du}{dx}&=\dfrac{2(x+3)-(2x+1)}{(x+3)^{2}}\\&=\dfrac{5}{(x+3)^{2}}\end{aligned}$
(a) The outer function is $y=u^{3}$.
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=3u^{2}\dfrac{du}{dx}\\&=3\left(\dfrac{2x+1}{x+3}\right)^{2}\dfrac{5}{(x+3)^{2}}\\&=\dfrac{15(2x+1)^{2}}{(x+3)^{4}}\end{aligned}$
(b) The outer function is $y=u^{1/2}$.
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=\dfrac{1}{2}u^{-1/2}\dfrac{du}{dx}\\&=\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{\sqrt{x+3}}{\sqrt{2x+1}}\dfrac{5}{(x+3)^{2}}\\&=\dfrac{5}{2\sqrt{2x+1}(x+3)\sqrt{x+3}}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: For $y=x(x-2)^{3}$, find (a) the gradient at $x=1$, (b) the equation of the tangent there and (c) the equation of the normal there.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The product and chain rules give
$\begin{aligned}y'&=(x-2)^{3}+3x(x-2)^{2}\\&=(x-2)^{2}[(x-2)+3x]\\&=2(x-2)^{2}(2x-1)\end{aligned}$
(a) At $x=1$, the gradient is $y'(1)=2$.
(b) The point of tangency is $(1,-1)$, since $y(1)=1(-1)^{3}=-1$.
$\begin{aligned}y+1&=2(x-1)\\y&=2x-3\end{aligned}$
(c) The normal has gradient $-\dfrac{1}{2}$.
$\begin{aligned}y+1&=-\dfrac{1}{2}(x-1)\\x+2y+1&=0\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Find all points on $y=x^{2}(x-2)^{2}$ where the tangent is horizontal.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The product and chain rules give
$\begin{aligned}y'&=2x(x-2)^{2}+2x^{2}(x-2)\\&=2x(x-2)[(x-2)+x]\\&=4x(x-2)(x-1)\end{aligned}$
For a horizontal tangent,
$\begin{aligned}4x(x-2)(x-1)&=0\\x&=0,\ 1,\ 2\end{aligned}$
$y(0)=0,\qquad y(1)=1,\qquad y(2)=0$.
The points are $(0,0)$, $(1,1)$ and $(2,0)$.

Separate the polynomial term:
$f(x)=x^{2}\sqrt{9-x^{2}}-3x^{3}$.
For the product, let $u=x^{2}$ and $v=\sqrt{9-x^{2}}$.
$u'=2x,\qquad v'=-\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{9-x^{2}}}$.
$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=u'v+uv'-9x^{2}\\&=2x\sqrt{9-x^{2}}-\dfrac{x^{3}}{\sqrt{9-x^{2}}}-9x^{2}\end{aligned}$

development.question_text: Differentiate $y = (x^{2} + 3)^{3}(3x - 4)^{4}$ using the product and chain rules.
Differentiate $y = \dfrac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 5}}$ using the quotient and chain rules.
Differentiate $y = \left(\dfrac{3x - 2}{2x + 5}\right)^{4}$ using the chain and quotient rules.
Differentiate $y = (4x + 3)\sqrt{2 - 3x}$ using the product and chain rules.
Differentiate $y = \dfrac{\sqrt{4x - 1}}{x + 3}$ using the quotient and chain rules.
Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y = x(x - 4)^{4}$ at $x = 3$.
Find all stationary points on the curve $y = x^{2}(3x - 7)^{3}$.
development.solution_text:
$y' = 2x(3x - 7)^{3} + 9x^{2}(3x - 7)^{2}$
$= x(3x - 7)^{2}[2(3x - 7) + 9x]$
$= x(3x - 7)^{2}(15x - 14)$
$\text{Setting } y' = 0 \text{ gives } x = 0, \quad x = \dfrac{14}{15}, \quad x = \dfrac{7}{3}$.
$\text{When } x = 0, y = 0$.
$\text{When } x = \dfrac{14}{15}, y = \left(\dfrac{14}{15}\right)^{2}\left(-\dfrac{21}{5}\right)^{3} = -\dfrac{201684}{3125}$.
$\text{When } x = \dfrac{7}{3}, y = 0$.
The stationary points are $(0,0)$, $\left(\dfrac{14}{15},-\dfrac{201684}{3125}\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{7}{3},0\right)$.

mastery.question_text: Differentiate $y = \sqrt{\dfrac{3x + 1}{x - 4}}$ using the chain and quotient rules for $x > 4$.
Find all points on the curve $y = x\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}$ where the tangent is horizontal.
mastery.solution_text:
$y' = 1\sqrt{4 - x^{2}} - \dfrac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}}$
$= \dfrac{4 - x^{2} - x^{2}}{\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}}$
$= \dfrac{4 - 2x^{2}}{\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}}$
$\text{Setting } y' = 0 \implies 4 - 2x^{2} = 0 \implies x = \pm \sqrt{2}$.
$\text{When } x = \sqrt{2}, y = \sqrt{2}\sqrt{2} = 2$.
$\text{When } x = -\sqrt{2}, y = -2$.
$(\sqrt{2}, 2) \text{ and } (-\sqrt{2}, -2)$
